evidence.quote: Let $A$ be a complex CM abelian variety.
It asserts algebraicity on the special fiber, not the Hodge conjecture for arbitrary complex abelian varieties.

exclusions.query: Hodge conjecture for arbitrary complex abelian varieties
exclusions.reason: The main cycle-class surjectivity assertion assumes CM; the specialization application proves algebraicity only on the special fiber.

evidence.quote:
For every integer $p\geq0$, the Betti cycle-class map $$\operatorname{cl}_B:\mathop{\mathrm{CH}}^p(A)_{\mathbb{Q}}
 \longrightarrow H^{2p}(A,\mathbb{Q})\cap H^{p,p}(A)$$ is surjective, where $\mathop{\mathrm{CH}}^p(A)_{\mathbb{Q}}=\mathop{\mathrm{CH}}^p(A)\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}}\mathbb{Q}$ and the intersection is taken in $H^{2p}(A,\mathbb{C})$.

exclusions.reason: The theorem uses rational Chow groups and rational cohomology; integral surjectivity is ABSENT.

evidence.quote: It does not assert generation of the Hodge ring on a fixed power by cup products of classes in codimensions one and two.

exclusions.query: Generation of a fixed-power Hodge ring by low-codimension classes
exclusions.reason: The reduction uses auxiliary products and contracts their intermediate factors; it does not assert the proposed fixed-power generation property.

evidence.quote: It does not assert that each Tate class lifts to a Hodge class on a single CM lifting, even up to isogeny

exclusions.query: A single CM lift for every finite-field Tate class
exclusions.reason: The cited implication compares motives and does not supply individual Hodge-class lifts on a single CM lifting.

evidence.quote: Suppose that an $L$-linear idempotent $p$ on $D_A\otimes_{\mathbb{Q}_q}L$ preserves the filtration and commutes with $\varphi_A\otimes1$.

exclusions.query: Pure Hodge filtration from a slope projector alone
exclusions.reason: The projector must preserve the Hodge filtration as well as commute with Frobenius; pure slope alone is insufficient.

evidence.quote: We do not claim it is holomorphic for such an intermediate parameter.

exclusions.query: Holomorphy of all intermediate rank-two variation forms
exclusions.reason: Holomorphy is established at rational endpoints after double alternation; the intermediate parameter forms are only asserted to be smooth.

evidence.quote: We first record how to work with individual embedding lines and recover rationality after extending coefficients.
We then construct the auxiliary CM varieties and assemble arbitrary balanced tensors from four-factor relations by algebraic correspondences.

prerequisites.concept: Rational CM sources of theta classes

evidence.quote: We calculate the active Hecke characters of the theta classes, insert them into that relation, and use degree-one Weil weight to isolate one Frobenius slope on every full character space.
The Hecke projectors preserve the Hodge filtration, so these slopes determine the Hodge types of all scalar conjugates.

prerequisites.concept: Generalized Hodge supports for CM varieties

evidence.quote: We will obtain such a support by algebraizing a Hodge map from an auxiliary CM abelian variety.

outputs.exact_statement:
Let $A$ be a complex CM abelian variety. For every integer $p\geq0$, the Betti cycle-class map $$\operatorname{cl}_B:\mathop{\mathrm{CH}}^p(A)_{\mathbb{Q}}
 \longrightarrow H^{2p}(A,\mathbb{Q})\cap H^{p,p}(A)$$ is surjective, where $\mathop{\mathrm{CH}}^p(A)_{\mathbb{Q}}=\mathop{\mathrm{CH}}^p(A)\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}}\mathbb{Q}$ and the intersection is taken in $H^{2p}(A,\mathbb{C})$. In particular, the rational Hodge conjecture holds in every codimension on every finite product of complex CM abelian varieties and on every power of such a product.

Let $T$ be a finite-dimensional rational vector space and $P\subset T_{\mathbb{C}}$ a complex-linear subspace. If $t\in T_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}}$ and $\sigma t\in P$ for every $\sigma\in\mathop{\mathrm{Gal}}(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}/\mathbb{Q})$, then $$t\in (T\cap P)\otimes_{\mathbb{Q}}\overline{\mathbb{Q}}.$$ The same assertion applies to the subspace of maps of any fixed Hodge type in a Hom space.

For a complex abelian variety $A$, the following conditions are equivalent:*

1.  *$J(H^1(A,\mathbb{Q}))$ is a torus.*

2.  *$H^1(A,\mathbb{Q})$ is a direct sum of rational Hodge structures, each of rank one over a CM field acting by Hodge endomorphisms.*

3.  *$\mathop{\mathrm{End}}(A)\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}}\mathbb{Q}$ contains a commutative semisimple algebra of rational dimension $2\dim A$.

Let $H$ and $H'$ be direct sums of rank-one weight-one Hodge modules over CM fields contained in $E$. Choose an embedding line $L\subset H_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}}$ and an embedding line $M\subset H'_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}}$ with the same complete type function. Extend any $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$-linear map $T:L\to M$ by zero on all other source embedding lines. Then $$T\in\mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}_{\mathrm{Hdg}}(H,H')\otimes_{\mathbb{Q}}\overline{\mathbb{Q}}.$$ When $H$ and $H'$ are degree-one cohomologies of abelian varieties, this map is therefore an algebraic-coefficient linear combination of pullbacks of abelian morphisms, up to rational denominators.

Let $E$ be a Galois CM field and let $v_1,v_2,v_3,v_4:G_E\to\{1,-1\}$ be odd sign functions satisfying $v_1+v_2=v_3+v_4$. Under the Künneth inclusion, the following line is algebraic: $$\label{eq:switch-line}
 U(v_1)_1\otimes U(v_2)_1\otimes U(v_3)_c\otimes U(v_4)_c
 \ \subset\
 H^4\!\left(\prod_{i=1}^4B(v_i),\overline{\mathbb{Q}}\right)$$
If Theorem 6 holds for every Galois CM field and every quadruple of odd sign functions satisfying its relation, then Theorem 1 holds.
It suffices to prove Theorem 6 when $s\geq2$ and $v_i(1)=1$ for all four functions.

For the symplectic space $(\mathbb V_P,\psi_P)$, restriction of the unitary splitting to $G(\mathbb{A}_F)$ yields an honest finite-adelic Weil action $\omega_{P,f}$. It is compatible with the rational covariance in Lemma 12 and is independent of the splitting characters. At infinity its half-determinant action is the natural action on $L^n$ in [eq:theta-halfdet].* *At a split finite place, choose as Schrödinger positions for a multiplicity line one standard three-dimensional embedding summand. The resulting $\mathop{\mathrm{SL}}_3$-action is inverse linear substitution. More generally, the normalized linear action associated with a transformation $h$ of the position space is $$\label{eq:theta-linear-action} (\rho(h)b)(x)=|\det h|^{-1/2}b(h^{-1}x).$$ A bare metaplectic lift outside $\mathop{\mathrm{SL}}_3$ is the normalized operator $\rho(h)$ times its lift scalar; that scalar must be retained in any use of such a lift.* *Every finite list of inputs is fixed under $\omega_{P,f}$ by all sufficiently deep principal lattice congruence subgroups.

For every finite input $\phi$, the form $\Theta_i(\phi)$ is holomorphic on $D$ and descends to every sufficiently deep principal congruence quotient. At any fixed point of $D$, the values $\Theta_i(\phi)$, as $\phi$ varies over finite Schwartz inputs, span the cotangent fiber. Finitely many actual inputs already span that fiber and descend at a common sufficiently deep principal level.

The rank-two construction has the following properties.*

1.  *At period data induced by a rational orthogonal decomposition $W=W_1\perp W_2$, the form $\Xi_W(\phi)$ is holomorphic. On a sufficiently deep common principal quotient it is a finite sum, with constant coefficients, of forms $\Theta_1(\phi_{1,r})\wedge\Theta_2(\phi_{2,r})$.*

2.  *There is an input which is a product in adapted rational coordinates and for which $\Xi_W(\phi)$ is nonzero.*

3.  *Fix $W$, the total finite input $\phi$, and a torsion-free principal quotient $X$ whose finite level fixes $\phi$ under $\omega_{W,f}$. With locally smooth constant-line trivializations, the map $$t\longmapsto\Xi_W(\phi;t)$$ is continuous in the $C^\infty$ topology of differential forms on this fixed compact quotient. The same finite level works throughout the parameter neighborhood.

The scheme $S$ is of finite type, smooth, and projective over $K_0$. Its complex connected components are compact ball quotients. For sufficiently divisible $N$, the component arising from $\Lambda$ is the quotient of $D$ by its principal special-unitary level.

After one finite extension of $K$ and removal of finitely many primes, the $S_j$ have smooth proper models with geometrically connected fibers, the $A_j$ extend to abelian schemes, and the $a_j$ extend to the models. The model of $S$ lies in the full tuple parameter scheme, retaining the $\mathcal O_E$-action and its graph coordinates. Differences of Albanese images generate every geometric fiber of each $A_j$.*

*At every remaining rational prime $q$ completely split in $K$, the ordinary locus of the universal abelian scheme is dense in each geometric component of the special fiber of $S$.

The rational spherical Hecke algebra of $(\mathscr G_q,\mathscr K_q)$ acts in $\mathop{\mathrm{End}}_K(A_S)\otimes\mathbb{Q}$ and, by pullback, on $H^1(S,\mathbb{Q})$. A basis operator in the positive range [eq:positive-hecke-range] is an integral homomorphism defined over $K$. Its pullback on one-forms is the sum of pullbacks over its target branches.

In the integral endomorphism ring of $\widetilde A_S$, $$\label{eq:albanese-frobenius-polynomial}
\Phi^3-D_1\Phi^2+qD_2\Phi-q^3D_3=0.$$

Every double coset in $\mathcal H_w^0$ has all its branches within each component of $S$. On the original ball component, its pullback action on theta classes is the inverse spherical action on the active local Weil input: a local double coset acts through its inverse.

Fix the input at all finite places other than $w$. There are $M>0$, an element $r\in E^\times$, and a nonzero algebraic number $\omega$ such that $$r\bar r=1,\qquad \operatorname{val}_{w}(r)=M,\qquad \operatorname{val}_{\bar w}(r)=-M,$$ with zero valuation at every other finite prime, and the map from radial inputs to theta one-form classes factors through $\mathcal D_q^M=\omega$. In the covariance convention of Lemma 12, $$\label{eq:radial-scalar-weight} \omega^2=\zeta\prod_{\tau\in\Sigma}\tau(r)^{-3d(\tau)}$$ for a root of unity $\zeta$. Every root of $X^M-\omega$ has absolute value one under every complex embedding.
The central operators $T_3$ and $C_0$ have finite order on the full tuple space $S$ and on $A_S$.

Let $\mathcal A/\mathbb{Z}_q$ be an abelian scheme with generic fiber $A$, and put $$D_A=H^1_{\mathrm{dR}}(A/\mathbb{Q}_q).$$ Equip $D_A$ with its Hodge filtration and its good-reduction crystalline Frobenius $\varphi_A$. Then $D_A$ is weakly admissible, its filtration has only indices $0$ and $1$, and endomorphisms extending over $\mathbb{Z}_q$ preserve the filtration and commute with $\varphi_A$.*

*Let $L/\mathbb{Q}_q$ be finite. Suppose that an $L$-linear idempotent $p$ on $D_A\otimes_{\mathbb{Q}_q}L$ preserves the filtration and commutes with $\varphi_A\otimes1$. If every Frobenius slope on its image is $t\in\{0,1\}$, then the induced filtration satisfies $$F^1\bigl(p(D_A\otimes L)\bigr)=
\begin{cases}
0,&t=0,\\
p(D_A\otimes L),&t=1.
\end{cases}$$

Let $\eta$ be an active numerical character with projective parameter $\{q^{1/2},q^{-1/2},e'\}$ supplied by Proposition 25 or by scalar conjugation, and put $$t_\eta=\frac12-\frac13\nu_\iota(e')\in\{0,1\}.$$ For every full numerical character $\chi$ extending $\eta$, the space $H_\chi\otimes_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}}\mathbb{C}$ is contained in $H^{1,0}(A_S)$ if $t_\eta=1$, and in $H^{0,1}(A_S)$ if $t_\eta=0$. Consequently $H^{\mathrm{act}}_\eta\otimes_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}}\mathbb{C}$ has the same pure Hodge type.

Fix $E,V,D,\Lambda$ and the principal lattice levels of Section 5. Let $v_1,\ldots,v_m:G_E\to\{1,-1\}$ be odd with $v_j(1)=1$. For each $j$, choose a finite family of finite adelic Schwartz inputs in the multiplicity-line construction $d_j(\tau)=v_j(\tau^{-1})$. Let $X_{\mathrm{base}}$ be a principal quotient at a torsion-free level in this framework. There is a common deeper principal cover $Y\to X_{\mathrm{base}}$, with $Y$ a smooth connected projective surface, on which every associated theta one-form class from the $j$-th family belongs to $$\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb{C}}\left\{ f\bigl(U(v_j)_1\bigr): f\in\mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}_{\mathrm{Hdg}}\bigl(U(v_j),H^1(Y,\mathbb{Q})\bigr) \right\}.$$ The maps are rational Hodge maps, with their images viewed after extension to $\mathbb{C}$. The conclusion persists after pullback to every deeper principal level. The auxiliary primes used for different $v_j$ may differ.

Let $W$ be a nonzero simple polarizable rational Hodge structure of CM type and weight $k$. Put $$r_0=\min\{p:W^{p,k-p}\ne0\},\qquad n=k-2r_0.$$ Then $n\ge0$, and there is a CM abelian variety $B$, possibly a point, and a surjective rational Hodge map $$H^n(B,\mathbb{Q})(-r_0)\longrightarrow W.$$

Let $A$ be a complex CM abelian variety. For integers $k,r\ge0$ and a rational Hodge substructure $W\subset H^k(A,\mathbb{Q})$ such that $W(r)$ is effective, there is a closed algebraic subset $Z\subset A$ of codimension at least $r$ such that $$W\subset\ker\bigl(H^k(A,\mathbb{Q})\longrightarrow
                         H^k(A\setminus Z,\mathbb{Q})\bigr).$$ This includes every finite product of CM abelian varieties and every power of such a product.

For every abelian variety $A/\mathbb{F}_q$, every integer $r\ge0$, and every prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(\mathbb{F}_q)$, the cycle-class map $$\mathop{\mathrm{CH}}^r(A)\otimes_\mathbb{Z}\mathbb{Q}_\ell\longrightarrow
 H^{2r}_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(\bar A,\mathbb{Q}_\ell(r))^{G_q}$$ is surjective. Numerical equivalence and $\ell$-adic homological equivalence coincide on rational algebraic cycles on $\bar A$.

Let $K$ be an algebraically closed field and $A/K$ an abelian variety of dimension $g$. For every prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(K)$, numerical and $\ell$-adic homological equivalence coincide on rational algebraic cycles on $A$. For every rational ample divisor class $h$ and every integer $0\le r\le g/2$, the rational symmetric form $$P_h^r(A)\times P_h^r(A)\longrightarrow\mathbb{Q},\qquad
 (x,y)\longmapsto(-1)^r\deg(xy\,h^{g-2r})$$ is positive definite after extension of scalars to $\mathbb{R}$. Thus the Hodge standard conjecture for $\ell$-adic étale cohomology holds for abelian varieties in arbitrary characteristic.
